title: You can have two Big Things, but not three: time-boxing a life and a startup
summary: Jason argues that a normal 24-hour day leaves room for roughly two time-consuming "Big Things" (job, kids, spouse, social life, major hobby, startup). Trying to hold three means one or more suffers, and you can't escape the limit by cutting sleep or by believing you're an exception.

principles.text: You get two Big Things in life, not three; pick which two.
principles.quote: The rule of life is: **You can have two "Big Things" in your life, but not three**.

principles.text: Big Things (job, kids, spouse, social life, hobby, startup) each need 40+ hours a week of concentrated time.
principles.quote: This is the amount of time it takes to tackle something huge. A career. A parent. A startup.

principles.text: Weekends and vacations don't add up to enough concentrated time to run a startup alongside a job and family.
principles.quote: There are weekends and vacations and sick days and such, but those don't add up to enough *concentrated* time to carry off something like a startup without causing work or home to suffer.

principles.text: A side-project startup on top of a day job costs you your family time, and sometimes the family itself.
principles.quote: You can do a startup on the side while you have a day job, but your family will never see you. You might even lose your family.

principles.text: Starting a company is easier before you have a family or even a spouse.
principles.quote: This is partly why it's easier to start a company before you have a family or even a spouse.

principles.text: Don't cut sleep to fit a third Big Thing; it degrades performance at everything.
principles.quote: cutting out sleep doesn't work--then you can't function at a high level at *anything*.
